The candidates are suggestions, not ground truth. Return exactly ONE decisions row per supplied candidate, using that identical name. Accept actual clear named identities; review genuinely ambiguous identities/spellings; reject generic filler, unsupported names and identity fragments. Use source spelling without guessing real-world corrections. Classify each with its most specific fitting supplied kind. organization is an institution, brand a commercial brand, service a named service, software a named software product, product_family a named hardware family, chip_model a specific processor, product a hardware model, technology a named method, standard a named standard. In a separate full-source sweep, add every eligible name missing from the supplied candidates to missingNames, with literal source name, disposition, kind and a brief reason. A singleton name is valid without agreement from another method. Do not invent sponsorship: an ad mention is still a name. Do not collapse separately named parents, families, models or versions. Never withhold a clear source-present name because of low importance. Set readComplete=true only when all supplied text and every candidate have been checked.
Lessons from development checker failures:
- Return bare named identities rather than grammatical wrappers. For a synthetic phrase like AeroWorks' RenderMax, reject the combined phrase as one keyword and retain AeroWorks and RenderMax separately if both are explicitly named. Possessives, generic hardware classes, usage clauses and website descriptions are not part of a name.
- A domain keyword is the literal host only. Reject a host combined with a URL path or neighboring spoken words; add the source-present host separately when missing.
- Do not invent an additional parent identity by cutting a word from a larger proper name. Retain a parent/family/base version when the source independently names that identity; preserve the full named model/version too. Generic chip/generation/hardware nouns are not product-name suffixes.
- Unfamiliar or noisy source spelling does not by itself make a clear intended name ineligible. Keep the literal source-spelled name when the context explicitly names a brand, service, laboratory, model or named standard; do not correct it from memory. Review a genuinely ambiguous namedness or boundary case instead of discarding it.
- Before finalizing, make a separate source sweep for brief comparisons, older models, advertising/payment-service names, interface-standard acronyms in any source case, and final words. Add missed names literally, without descriptions or guessed aliases.

extractorLessons: A name may contain spaces, hyphens, mixed case, digits, dots, slashes, and version suffixes; treat the full contiguous written form as one name.
Attribution words such as possessives or 'use of' are not part of the named thing; capture the owner/company and the product/feature/technology separately when both are named.
For URLs/domains, the domain is a name; do not merge domain and path or surrounding words into one name.
Coordination and lists contain multiple names; split on punctuation and conjunctions while preserving each complete name.
Do not emit articles, pronouns, prepositions, conjunctions, adverbs, adjectives, ordinary verbs, generic category nouns, standalone units, or number+unit measurement phrases as names.
Do not emit partial tokens from a compound identity; emit the longest contiguous named expression unless the text clearly presents two independent names.
Keep near-identical model/version spellings distinct exactly as written; do not normalize spelling, spacing, capitalization, or version punctuation.
Do not require prominence or repetition; include single occurrences, including brand/company names in sponsor reads and domains in calls to action.
